- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries, the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`), plus a separate build (`vite.site.config.ts`) that prerenders the landing page (`site.html`, `src/site/`) into `dist-site`.
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*`, Alchemy, or Foldkit, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` in the environment. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking
- [Merge own PRs](merge-own-prs.md) — squash-merge my green PRs in surveybeat-next without asking

# A test Invitation is its own token kind, and its answers are never saved

A Lead or Organization admin can send themselves a test of a Pulse from the Pulse editor (issue #136). The test is the real Invitation email in the sender's language, with "Test" in the subject, the same one-tap rating links, and the real answer page. The flow runs to the end, including the "Your Lead will see: …" preview and the thank-you screen, but it stores no Submission, no Answer, and no Participation record, so nothing reaches Results, Comment themes, or member history. This amends the ADR 0005 flow for one new token kind. It does not weaken A1–A10.

**Token kind.**
- A test token is derived from `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` like an Invitation token, but under its own label: `test-invitation:v1:<pulseId>:<personId>:<testId>`, where `testId` is random per send. A test token can therefore never equal an Invitation token, and the key still never leaves the Worker environment.
- Only the token's hash is stored, in its own D1 table `test_invitation_index` (hash, Organization, Pulse, expiry). It is never written to `invitation_index`, and the Organization has no Invitation row for it. A test token expires 7 days after it is sent.
- The Organization stores only the send in `test_send` (send id, Person, Pulse, token hash, time) for the rate limit and for the Queue consumer to index the token once the email is sent, as it does for Invitations. Rows older than 7 days are deleted.

**Answering with a test token.**
- `/exchange` resolves `invitation_index` first. A miss falls back to `test_invitation_index`, and the Organization builds the context from the Pulse's saved Questions and settings, with `test: true`, no Round, `hasAnswered: false`, and the expiry as close time.

1	# A test Invitation is its own token kind, and its answers are never saved
2	
3	A Lead or Organization admin can send themselves a test of a Pulse from the Pulse editor (issue #136). The test is the real Invitation email in the sender's language, with "Test" in the subject, the same one-tap rating links, and the real answer page. The flow runs to the end, including the "Your Lead will see: …" preview and the thank-you screen, but it stores no Submission, no Answer, and no Participation record, so nothing reaches Results, Comment themes, or member history. This amends the ADR 0005 flow for one new token kind. It does not weaken A1–A10.
4	
5	**Token kind.**
6	- A test token is derived from `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` like an Invitation token, but under its own label: `test-invitation:v1:<pulseId>:<personId>:<testId>`, where `testId` is random per send. A test token can therefore never equal an Invitation token, and the key still never leaves the Worker environment.
7	- Only the token's hash is stored, in its own D1 table `test_invitation_index` (hash, Organization, Pulse, expiry). It is never written to `invitation_index`, and the Organization has no Invitation row for it. A test token expires 7 days after it is sent.
8	- The Organization stores only the send in `test_send` (send id, Person, Pulse, token hash, time) for the rate limit and for the Queue consumer to index the token once the email is sent, as it does for Invitations. Rows older than 7 days are deleted.
9	
10	**Answering with a test token.**
11	- `/exchange` resolves `invitation_index` first. A miss falls back to `test_invitation_index`, and the Organization builds the context from the Pulse's saved Questions and settings, with `test: true`, no Round, `hasAnswered: false`, and the expiry as close time.
12	- `/first-answer` with a test token applies every check the real route applies (body-only credentials, A5, Edit key hash format). It then redacts the comment as the real path would, returns `{ saved: true, shownToLead }`, and writes nothing to the Organization. It records the Edit key hash in D1's `test_submission_index` (hash, Organization, Pulse, expiry), never in `submission_index`.
13	- `/answer` resolves `submission_index` first. A miss falls back to `test_submission_index`, and the answer is redacted and discarded the same way.
14	- The routes that write Submissions and Participation records (`recordFirstAnswer`, `saveAnswer`) are reachable only through `invitation_index` and `submission_index`, so a test token or a test Edit key cannot write a real answer. The privacy suite proves it.
15	- The answer page shows "This is a test. Your answers aren't saved." It keeps the test Edit key in memory only and does not keep the answers in the browser, so the member history page (ADR 0017) never shows a test.
16	
17	**Who and how often.** Whoever may edit the Pulse (the Team's Lead and Organization admins, `team.editPulse`) may send a test, to their own address only. The Organization refuses a sixth send by the same Person within an hour. Non-production stages capture the email in D1, as for every other email.
18	
19	## Considered options
20	
21	- **A test Round with real Invitations, deleted afterwards.** Rejected: it would write Participation records and Submissions, and any missed cleanup leaks into Results and response rates.
22	- **A flag on the Invitation token or on `invitation_index`.** Rejected: one missed check would let a test write a real answer. Separate tables make the real write path unreachable.
23	- **Opening the answer page with a preview flag and no email.** Rejected: the Lead wants to see exactly what members get, including the email and its one-tap links.
24	
25	## Consequences
26	
27	- The Submission Worker reads two more D1 tables, and both hold hashes only, with no Person.
28	- Test answers are lost by design. The Lead cannot see them, and neither can anyone else.
29	- `test_send` stores a Person and a time, but nothing about answers.

Verdict: no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings in S2a. I ran `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/PulsesApi.test.ts packages/domain/src/pulses`: 103 tests passed. I did not run the workerd test in `Organization.test.ts`.

**What I checked and found sound**
- **Recipient:** the address comes from `person.email` for the session's `actorId` (Editor.ts `decideTestSend`, Organization.ts around lines 1357-1420). The request carries no address, so a test cannot go to another address.
- **Team scoping:** `decideTestSend` calls `authorize(... "team.editPulse", teamId)` and then `findPulse(state, teamId, pulseId)`. A Lead of another Team gets Forbidden, and a Pulse reached through the wrong Team gets 404. `PulsesApi.test.ts` covers both cases.
- **Rate limit:** the count, the insert, `sends.create` and the cleanup all run inside one `sql.withTransaction`, in a single-threaded Durable Object. The limit check is therefore atomic, with no race.
- **Token:** `test_send` and `getTestSendBySendId` hold only the hash. The raw token is derived at render time and never returned or logged; the API returns only `{ email }`.
- **Index isolation:** the EmailDelivery.ts `else` branch writes only to `test_invitation_index`, never to `invitation_index`.
- **Test route exposure:** it is registered inside the `isTestStage(stage)` block and in the test-only route list.
- **Other items:** the same-origin check is in place, `PrivacyRegistry` is classified, and `RemovePerson` deletes the Person's `test_send` rows.
- **Lint rules:** `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` has no rule that references the new tables.

**Findings**

1. MINOR: `packages/cloudflare/src/EmailDelivery.ts`, the new `else` branch. It indexes the test token whenever the state is not `Failed`, so `Pending` and `Sending` also pass. ADR 0021 says "once the email is sent". A retry-pending send would have its token indexed before delivery. This is harmless, because the email never arrives and the token is unguessable. Narrow it to `result.state._tag === "Sent"` to match the ADR, unless you intentionally mirror the Invitation behaviour.

2. MINOR: same branch. Every non-Invitation send (sign-in, welcome and so on) now makes an extra Durable Object RPC, `getTestSendBySendId`. Consider branching on the stored email's `_tag === "TestInvitationEmail"`, or accept the cost knowingly.

3. MINOR: `sendTestInvitation` in `packages/domain/src/pulses/PulseFlow.ts` records the send, and the `test_send` row counts towards the limit, before `EmailOutbox.queue` runs. If queueing fails, the Person loses a slot and no email goes out. This is the same pattern as the other sends, so it is acceptable. It is worth a comment at most.

4. MINOR: after `RemovePerson`, a still-valid `test_invitation_index` row remains in D1 for up to 7 days. It holds only the hash, the Pulse and the Organization, and no Person. This is consistent with the ADR, but the ADR should state it as intended.

5. MINOR: test coverage gaps.
   - The in-memory `sendTest` in `packages/cloudflare/src/auth/testing.ts` uses `actions: []`, so it does not cover the eligible-Actions path.
   - Nothing tests the 7-day `test_send` cleanup, or `RemovePerson` deleting `test_send` rows.
   - The workerd test also fixes `now` at 1_700_000_000_000 and passes `now` into the Durable Object, so the window logic is exercised only through that explicit argument.
